answer: Time-locked task bonds resist Sybil attacks: a new identity posts a bond that only unlocks after completing a chain of verified useful tasks spread over days, like a falcon proving itself across repeated hunts rather than one flight. The bond is a marble every identity must carry — one marble per agent, no bulk discount — and it is slashed if the identity misbehaves. An attacker facing an ocean of honest work must fund and wait out a bond for every fake, so a thousand aliases cost a thousand bonds and a thousand waiting periods, while one honest agent pays once.
